claims.text: Common steel or existing-alloy equipment components corrode rapidly during direct contact with high-temperature liquid aluminum.
A dense, inert ceramic coating can protect dipping and plating equipment from molten-aluminum corrosion.
A tungsten-based cermet coating can protect dipping and plating equipment from molten-aluminum corrosion.
Thermal spraying can be used to apply the proposed protective coating to the substrate.
Laser cladding can be used to apply the proposed protective coating to the substrate.
A fully dense and adherent coating acts as a barrier to liquid-aluminum infiltration.
A fully dense and adherent coating acts as a barrier to chemical attack by molten aluminum.
The proposed ceramic or cermet coating is inert and forms a stable, non-reactive diffusion barrier.
The diffusion barrier prevents chemical reactions between molten aluminum and the substrate.
Suppressing reactions and aluminum infiltration reduces corrosion and wear during prolonged exposure.
Coated components will have a significantly lower corrosion rate than uncoated components.
Coated components will exhibit less weight loss and surface degradation than uncoated components.
The coating will extend component service life relative to uncoated parts.
Protection depends on maintaining coating density and adhesion under cyclic thermal and mechanical stresses.
Cracking, degradation, or delamination of the coating will diminish protection.
